gaps.sentence: The winners ___ (GIVE) their medals by the mayor last night.
gaps.explanation: 'Last night' + agent 'by the mayor': past simple passive were given.

gaps.sentence: The village ___ (reach) by road until 1962; only mules could make the climb.
gaps.explanation: 'Until 1962' describes a past state of affairs: could not be + past participle.

gaps.sentence: This form ___ (sign) in ink — digital signatures aren't valid.
gaps.explanation: Modal passive: modal + be + past participle. Obligation: must (also has to) be signed.
'By + future time' signals future perfect passive: will have been + processed.

gaps.sentence: Historic documents ___ (digitise) right now, which is why the archive is shut.
gaps.hint: action in progress now, plural subject
gaps.explanation: Present continuous passive: are being + digitised for an action happening around now.

gaps.sentence: Hamlet ___ (perform) almost continuously since it was written.
gaps.explanation: 'Since + past clause' requires present perfect passive: has been + performed.

gaps.sentence: A cheaper version of the vaccine ___ right now.
gaps.explanation: 'Right now' requires present continuous passive: is being + developed.

gaps.sentence: The missing manuscripts ___ (find) — the search is officially over.
gaps.explanation: Present perfect passive: have/has been + past participle. The result matters now.
